issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s permanent structural alterations that substantially diminish a rented building’s value or utility constitute a ground for eviction.
material_facts: The tenants removed the original roofs, partition walls and doors of several shops, replaced the roofs, and merged the shops with the adjoining verandah, changing the premises’ layout and character.
The tenants demolished part of a boundary wall, created access from adjoining property, and constructed a room and staircase.
Inspection reports, witness testimony and municipal notices supported the finding that the alterations had been made by the tenants.
Even assuming the landlord had consented to construction of a shed over part of the open land, the remaining permanent alterations to the shops and verandah were not covered by that consent.
issues.conclusion: The permanent alterations were acts likely to impair materially the value or utility of the premises, viewed from the landlords’ perspective. The eviction application was allowed; the tenants were directed to vacate, subject to a temporary opportunity to remain upon furnishing an undertaking.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 13(2)(iii) of the East Punjab Rent Restriction Act, 1949, a tenant is liable to eviction for acts likely to impair materially the value or utility of the building or rented land. “Impair materially” means a substantial diminution in quality, strength or value, assessed by comparing the premises before and after the alterations. The assessment is from the landlord’s point of view, as stated in Vipin Kumar v. Roshan Lal Anand, (1993) 2 SCC 614. Whether the alterations materially impair value or utility is a mixed question of law and fact; the nature and permanence of the construction are relevant.

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction of a tenant from rented premises.
predicates.tenant_made_permanent_structural_changes: The tenant made permanent structural changes to the rented premises, including removing and replacing structural elements and changing the layout.
predicates.alterations_substantially_impair_value_o: The changes substantially diminished the premises’ value or utility when assessed from the landlord’s point of view.

issues.definition: When a tenant in an eviction proceeding makes permanent structural changes that substantially impair the premises’ value or utility from the landlord’s point of view, the eviction application is allowed.
